note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 3.11.5: 'To forward Path and PathTear messages, an RSVP process must be able to query the routing process(s) for routes.' Single-polarity capability. TestIntegrationRSVPPathCarriage sends PATH and PathTear through SendPath and fails unless the frame's L2 destination is the explicit hop. TestIntegrationRSVPPathAvoidsDataFEC resolves through production ResolveRoute with an MPLS data FEC installed and fails unless PATH leaves unlabelled to the selected hop with source, destination, TTL and interface intact. Residual: that unit still skips on EOPNOTSUPP/ENOENT when the running kernel lacks MPLS_IPTUNNEL, and now runs on the host kernel rather than the Ze guest; the requirement does not depend on it alone.
